name: Forensics: Read the Manual
problem_statement: Directive: There is a file called `instructions.txt`. Read what is inside it to find the flag.

hints.text: In Linux, the `cat` command reads files. Type `cat instructions.txt` and hit run.

name: Query: Open the Box
problem_statement: Directive: The database has a table named `vault`. Look inside to find the hidden code.

hints.text: SQL uses SELECT. Type `SELECT * FROM vault` to see everything, then read the table output.

name: OSINT: The Sticky Note
problem_statement: Directive: The suspect left a sticky note on their digital desktop. The password is right there.

hints.text: Look really closely at the ASCII art sticky note rendered on the right pane.

name: Forensics: What's in here?
problem_statement: Directive: You are in a secure folder. What files are in here? Find the file named 'flag_xxx'.

hints.text: Type `ls` (which stands for list) and hit run to see all the files in the directory.

name: Query: The Target
problem_statement: Directive: Look at the `agents` table. Find the name of the agent whose `status` is 'Rogue'.

hints.text: Type `SELECT * FROM agents`. Scan the list on the right for the rogue agent's name.

name: OSINT: The Archived Pin
problem_statement: Directive: The agent's old ID card is in this archived web page text. Find the 4-digit ID.

hints.text: Just read the text block on the right pane carefully. Look for the phrase 'Legacy Pin'.

evidence_board.content:
IdeaLab Member Profile

Name: Kabir

Status: Inactive

Legacy Pin: 4520

name: Forensics: Who am I?
problem_statement: Directive: The system needs to verify your terminal username.

hints.text: Linux has a literal command for this. Type `whoami` and hit run.

name: Query: Filter the Noise
problem_statement: Directive: The `inventory` table is huge. Get only the item where the `id` is exactly 77.

hints.text: Use a WHERE clause! Type `SELECT * FROM inventory WHERE id = 77`.

name: OSINT: The Metadata
problem_statement: Directive: We extracted the raw EXIF data from a photograph. What camera model took this photo?

hints.text: Look at the raw metadata text block on the right. Find the line labeled 'Camera Model'.

evidence_board.content:
Filename: IMG_9921.CR2
Date Taken: 2024-10-15
Camera Maker: Canon
Camera Model: EOS_5D
Focal Length: 50mm

name: Forensics: Echo Chamber
problem_statement: Directive: Make the terminal repeat the word 'SGSITS' back to you to unlock the system.

hints.text: The `echo` command prints text. Type `echo SGSITS`.

name: Query: Count the Spies
problem_statement: Directive: How many total spies are registered in the `spies` table?

hints.text: SQL can count for you. Type `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM spies`.

name: OSINT: The Fake Website
problem_statement: Directive: Look at the raw HTML source code on the right. What is the hidden comment?

hints.text: In HTML, developer comments are invisible on the actual website and look like `<!-- secret text -->`.

name: Forensics: Where am I?
problem_statement: Directive: You are lost deep in a folder structure. Print your current working directory to get the flag.

hints.text: The command for 'Print Working Directory' is just its initials: `pwd`.

name: Query: The Richest
problem_statement: Directive: Find the absolute highest balance in the `accounts` table.

hints.text: SQL has a MAX function. Type `SELECT MAX(balance) FROM accounts`.

name: OSINT: Domain Age
problem_statement: Directive: Look at the WHOIS domain data on the right. What year was this website registered?

hints.text: Scan the text block for 'Creation Date' or 'Registered On'.

evidence_board.content:
Domain Name: SYNDICATE-NET.ORG
Registry Domain ID: 987654321_DOMAIN_ORG-VRSN
Creation Date: 2018-06-15T12:00:00Z
Registrar: NameCheap, Inc.

name: Forensics: The Hidden Payload
problem_statement: Directive: The current directory appears completely empty when you type `ls`, but a concealed script is present. Find its exact filename.

hints.text: In Linux systems, files starting with a dot (.) are hidden. Add the `-a` (all) flag: type `ls -a`.

name: Query: Sort it Out
problem_statement: Directive: Query the `agents` table. Who is the agent that appears at the very top of the list when sorted alphabetically by `last_name`?

hints.text: You need to order the results. Add `ORDER BY last_name ASC` to your SELECT statement.

name: Forensics: Searching Inside
problem_statement: Directive: The `server.log` file has 10,000 lines. Find the exact 4-digit code attached to the phrase 'CRITICAL_FAIL:'.

hints.text: You don't need to read the whole file. Use the grep command to search inside it: `grep "CRITICAL_FAIL" server.log`.

name: Query: Combine Two Tables
problem_statement: Directive: `employees` has names. `access_logs` has entry times. Find the name of the employee who entered at '03:00:00'.

hints.text: Combine them using JOIN! `SELECT name FROM employees JOIN access_logs ON employees.id = access_logs.emp_id WHERE time = '03:00:00'`.

name: OSINT: Hex Editor
problem_statement: Directive: We ran a file through a Hexadecimal reader. It reveals a hidden text string appended at the very end of the file. Find it.

hints.text: Scroll to the absolute bottom of the text-based Hex dump on the right pane. Look at the readable ASCII letters on the far right column.

name: Forensics: The Tail End
problem_statement: Directive: The system is actively writing to `stream.log`. Read only the very last line of the file to get the flag.

hints.text: The `tail` command outputs the end of a file. Try `tail -n 1 stream.log`.

name: Query: Unique Values
problem_statement: Directive: There are duplicate entries. Find the total number of completely *unique* `city` names in the `safehouses` table.

hints.text: Use the `DISTINCT` keyword right after SELECT to ignore duplicates. `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT city) FROM safehouses;`

name: OSINT: The Network Hop
problem_statement: Directive: We ran a `traceroute` to find where the signal is bouncing. Look at the terminal output on the right. What is the IP address of the 4th hop?

hints.text: Find line number 4 in the text output. The IP address looks like `192.168.x.x`.

name: Forensics: The Symbolic Link
problem_statement: Directive: The file `shortcut.lnk` is pointing to another location. Find the absolute path of the original file it points to.

hints.text: Use `ls -l`. The output will show an arrow `->` pointing to the real file path.

name: Query: The Null Protocol
problem_statement: Directive: The database crashed. Find the `badge_id` in the `access_logs` table where the `timestamp` is exactly NULL.

hints.text: You cannot use `=` for NULL in SQL. You must use `WHERE timestamp IS NULL`.

name: Query: The Grand Heist (Triple Join)
problem_statement: Directive: `suspects` has IDs. `vehicles` links IDs to plates. `toll_booths` links plates to cities. Find the `city` of the suspect named 'Kabir'.

hints.text: Double JOIN required. Join suspects to vehicles on `suspect_id`. Then join toll_booths on `license_plate`. Filter `WHERE name = 'Kabir'`.

name: Forensics: Piped Count
problem_statement: Directive: The `auth.log` file tracks all logins. Write a command chain to count exactly how many times the word 'Failed' appears.

hints.text: You can pipe (`|`) commands into each other! Read the file, filter for the specific word, and count the lines: `cat auth.log | grep "Failed" | wc -l`.

name: Query: Above Average
problem_statement: Directive: Query the `salaries` table. Find the `name` of the operative who earns strictly more than the overall average salary of the entire organization.

hints.text: You need a subquery! First find the average `(SELECT AVG(salary) FROM salaries)`, then use that in your main WHERE clause.

name: OSINT: Wireshark Packet Dump
problem_statement: Directive: Analyze the raw HTTP PCAP (packet capture) text dump. An operative logged into an unsecured HTTP site. Extract their plaintext password.

hints.text: Search the raw text block on the right for `POST` requests. Look for the payload body containing `password=`.

evidence_board.content:
GET /index.html HTTP/1.1
Host: secure.local

POST /login.php HTTP/1.1
Host: secure.local
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

user=admin&password=Hunter2

name: Forensics: Base64 Decode
problem_statement: Directive: The file `encoded_flag.txt` contains a Base64 string. Decode it directly in the terminal to reveal the plaintext flag.

hints.text: Pipe the `cat` command into the base64 decoding tool: `cat encoded_flag.txt | base64 -d`.

name: Forensics: Hidden History
problem_statement: Directive: An operator executed a critical command and cleared their terminal, but bash records prior keystrokes in a hidden dotfile. Inspect the bash history file to recover the authorization flag.

hints.text: Inspect the hidden bash history file using `cat ~/.bash_history` or `cat .bash_history`.

name: Network: HTTP Header Snooping
problem_statement: Directive: A staging web service on `http://127.0.0.1:8080/health` returns custom telemetry headers. Use curl to inspect the response headers and find the value of `X-Service-Flag`.

hints.text: Use the `-I` or `-i` flag with curl to dump response headers: `curl -I http://127.0.0.1:8080/health`.

name: Forensics: Secret in the Subdir
problem_statement: Directive: A nested configuration directory exists under `/var/configs`. Find all files ending in `.conf` recursively and locate the token stored in the `auth.conf` file.

hints.text: Use `find /var/configs -name "*.conf"` to locate the configuration files, then `cat` the file.

name: Forensics: Pattern Harvester
problem_statement: Directive: The file `system_events.log` contains thousands of lines. Search for lines containing the keyword 'FLAG:' to extract the security token.

hints.text: Use `grep "FLAG:" system_events.log` to isolate the line containing the token.

name: Forensics: Modified in the Shadows
problem_statement: Directive: An adversary altered a file in `/opt/data` today. List the files sorted by modification time to identify the most recently updated file.

hints.text: Use `ls -lt` to sort directory contents by modification time descending.

name: Forensics: Hidden Under the Dot
problem_statement: Directive: A covert operative hid a file whose name begins with a dot in `/tmp/staging`. Discover the hidden filename and view its content.

hints.text: List hidden files with `ls -la /tmp/staging`, then read the dotfile with `cat`.

name: Network: Hostname Resolution
problem_statement: Directive: Inspect `/etc/hosts` to find the static IP address mapped to the internal host `telemetry.internal.corp`.

hints.text: Print the contents of the hosts resolution file with `cat /etc/hosts`.

name: Forensics: Counting Lines
problem_statement: Directive: The audit file `audit.csv` lists detected security alerts. Count how many total lines are in `audit.csv`.

hints.text: Use `wc -l audit.csv` to count the lines in the file.

name: Forensics: Environment Variable Peek
problem_statement: Directive: The container runtime passed an operational secret in an environment variable named `MISSION_TOKEN`. Print its value.

hints.text: Print an environment variable using `echo $MISSION_TOKEN` or `env | grep MISSION_TOKEN`.

name: Forensics: File Size Triage
problem_statement: Directive: Several dump files were created in `/var/dumps`. Locate the only dump file that is not 0 bytes and read the string within.

hints.text: Use `find /var/dumps -size +0c` or `ls -lh /var/dumps` to spot the non-empty file.

name: Forensics: SUID Binary Hunt
problem_statement: Directive: An attacker planted an executable binary with SUID bit (permissions 4755) in `/usr/local/bin`. Find the name of the SUID binary.

hints.text: Use `find /usr/local/bin -perm -4000` to enumerate binaries with the SUID bit set.

name: Forensics: Access Log 404 Hunter
problem_statement: Directive: Analyze `access.log` to find the URI path that returned HTTP status code 404 during an automated scanning probe.

hints.text: Filter lines containing ' 404 ' using grep or awk: `grep " 404 " access.log`.

name: Forensics: Scheduled Cron Job
problem_statement: Directive: Examine system scheduled tasks in `/etc/crontab` and `/etc/cron.d/` to find the script executed every 5 minutes by the root user.

hints.text: View `/etc/crontab` and check the cron expression `*/5 * * * *`.

name: Query: Schema Table Discovery
problem_statement: Directive: Query `sqlite_master` in the database to discover the name of the hidden audit table that begins with `shadow_`.

hints.text: Execute `SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name LIKE 'shadow_%';`.

workspace.default_query: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table';

name: Forensics: Grep Regex IP Extraction
problem_statement: Directive: A rogue server transmitted connection attempts logged in `firewall.log`. Use extended grep with regex to extract IPv4 addresses matching subnet `10.50.X.X`.

hints.text: Use `grep -E "10\.50\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+" firewall.log` or `grep "10.50." firewall.log`.

name: Forensics: World-Writable Audit
problem_statement: Directive: Audit permissions in `/opt/services` to find the world-writable file (permission mode 777 or o+w) that represents a privilege escalation hazard.

hints.text: Use `find /opt/services -perm -0002` or `ls -l` and look for `rwxrwxrwx`.

name: Network: Listening Socket Audit
problem_statement: Directive: Inspect the system socket status output from `ss -tulpn` or `netstat -tlpn` to find the unauthenticated service listening on port 9090.

hints.text: Search for `:9090` in the socket listing output to identify the program name.

name: Query: SQL Injection Probe
problem_statement: Directive: In the `audit_trail` table, multiple suspicious SQL injection payloads were logged. Query the payload that successfully extracted admin credentials.

hints.text: Use `SELECT * FROM audit_trail WHERE payload LIKE '%UNION%' OR status = 'EXPLOITED';`.

name: Forensics: SSH Authorized Keys Audit
problem_statement: Directive: Investigate `/home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys` to identify the rogue public key comment appended by an unauthorized actor.

hints.text: Read the authorized_keys file: `cat /home/deploy/.ssh/authorized_keys` and examine the trailing comment.

name: Forensics: Defective Systemd Unit
problem_statement: Directive: A persistent service was installed in `/etc/systemd/system/malware.service`. Inspect the `ExecStart` directive to discover what binary is executed.

hints.text: Print the unit file with `cat /etc/systemd/system/malware.service` and read `ExecStart=`.

name: Forensics: Pipeline Awk Aggregator
problem_statement: Directive: A high-volume access log `web_traffic.csv` records IP addresses in column 1 and bytes in column 4. Write an awk command to sum total bytes for IP `192.168.1.50`.

hints.text: Chain awk with pattern match and accumulator: `awk -F',' '$1=="192.168.1.50"{sum+=$4} END{print sum}' web_traffic.csv`.

name: Network: DNS Tunneling Exfiltration
problem_statement: Directive: An adversary exfiltrated base64 data chunks encoded in DNS query subdomains in `dns_queries.log`. Concatenate the subdomains for domain `corp-exfil.xyz` and decode them.

hints.text: Extract subdomain prefixes using `awk` or `cut`, strip `.corp-exfil.xyz`, concatenate, and pipe through `base64 -d`.

name: Forensics: Memory String Carving
problem_statement: Directive: Carve ASCII strings from a raw physical memory dump `memdump.raw` looking for decrypted cryptographic master keys prefixed with `MASTER_KEY:`.

hints.text: Extract printable strings using `strings memdump.raw | grep "MASTER_KEY:"`.

name: Network: PCAP TLS Handshake SNI
problem_statement: Directive: Analyze the captured TLS Client Hello packets in `traffic_capture.pcap.txt` to find the Server Name Indication (SNI) hostname used by the covert command-and-control server.

hints.text: Search packet dissections for `Server Name:` or `Handshake: Client Hello` with `grep -A 2 "Server Name"`.

name: Forensics: Chained Sed and Xargs
problem_statement: Directive: A list of candidate artifact file paths is stored in `file_manifest.txt`. Strip leading whitespace with sed, and pass existing paths via xargs to grep for `FLAG_SIG`.

hints.text: Use `sed 's/^[ 	]*//' file_manifest.txt | xargs grep "FLAG_SIG"`.

name: Network: Topology Reconstruction
problem_statement: Directive: A multi-hop routing table `routing_table.txt` defines network gateways. Trace the next-hop router gateway IP for destination subnet `172.28.0.0/16`.

hints.text: Search routing table for destination `172.28.0.0` and identify the Gateway column.

name: Forensics: Multi-Stage Hex Carving
problem_statement: Directive: An obfuscated shell payload in `corrupt_firmware.bin` contains an embedded tar archive offset starting at magic bytes `75 73 74 61 72` (ustar). Extract the header token.

hints.text: Use `xxd` or `hexdump -C corrupt_firmware.bin | grep -C 2 "ustar"` to locate the offset and token.

name: Forensics: Inode Link Investigation
problem_statement: Directive: An operative hardlinked a sensitive file to disguise it. Find all file paths sharing inode number `849201` in directory `/var/vault`.

hints.text: Use `find /var/vault -inum 849201` to find all directory entries linking to the same inode.

name: Network: TCP Session Stream Assembly
problem_statement: Directive: A fragmented Telnet session was captured in `telnet_stream.dump`. Assemble the sequence of retransmitted characters to reconstruct the administrator authentication command.

hints.text: Sort the stream packets by sequence number: `sort -k2,2n telnet_stream.dump | awk '{print $4}' | tr -d '\n'`.

name: Forensics: Multi-Stage Forensic Vault
problem_statement: Directive: A multi-layered artifact `vault_stage1.txt` contains a base64 encoded string, which decodes to a reverse-rot13 command. Execute the pipeline to unlock the master flag.

hints.text: Decode base64 first (`base64 -d vault_stage1.txt`), then pipe through rot13 with `tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m'`.
